metadata.title: Soil Carbon Sequestration Impacts on Global Climate Change and Food Security

summary: Landmark paper by Rattan Lal detailing carbon dynamics, rainfall use efficiency, and restoration of depleted dryland soils.

sections.text: Agricultural soils in dryland and semi-arid ecosystems contain severely depleted SOC pools, often less than 0.5%. Adoption of restorative practices such as conservation tillage, mulching, and legume cover cropping enhances rainfall use efficiency, reduces erosion, and rebuilds the soil biological community.

The critical limit of SOC in low-rainfall tropical and subtropical regions is approximately 1.1%. Below this threshold, soil structural decline accelerates, leading to surface crusting and elevated runoff losses during sudden rainfall events.
